summary: The paper gives two ways to run the iterations of a DO loop nest concurrently: a hyperplane method for asynchronous multiprocessors and array computers, and a coordinate method for synchronous single-instruction-stream machines. It counts the sequential steps each method needs for example loops and reports only preliminary compiler experience.
why_read: It shows how a compiler can rewrite a loop nest so that its iterations run in parallel while the order of references to the same array element is preserved.
main_contribution: Two loop-rewriting methods, each with conditions that keep results unchanged, including a linear-mapping construction for choosing the parallel planes.
main_limitation: The evaluation is analytic iteration counts and qualitative compiler experience with no measured run times, and the general optimal mapping has no known practical method.
evaluation_method: analytic counts of sequential iterations for example loops; no measurements
notes: Title capitalization differs: the PDF prints 'The Parallel Execution of DO Loops' and the catalog has 'The parallel execution of DO loops'. First author (Leslie Lamport) and year (1974) match.
